gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UPS Harman lab-tested for its pellet stoves, the APC BE750G, switches to battery in 6 ms typical and 10 ms maximum. That is the only stove-validated transfer time we have. A power station that switches in ≤10 ms is inside it, and the 15–20 ms units are outside anything Harman tested.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: our own current page, the Harman HAR-0040U PDF (cited; its contents as quoted by Power Fallback) and WattMatrix (cited, but it now returns 404). I also compared against the top uncited pages, powerfallback.com and homebatteryreport.com. The Harman PDF and Power Fallback already cover the decisive mechanism: Harman controls are 'pre-set for quick shutdown', a UPS gives 'safe shut-down only', and a dealer must set Continue Operation (dip switch #4 on knob boards). They also cover pure sine wave. None of them gives a transfer-time number that a stove has been shown to tolerate. Power Fallback 'gives no specific transfer-time threshold'. Home Battery Report lists the power stations' ms figures and names the approved APC BE750G and Tripp Lite INTERNET750U, but never states those UPSs' own transfer times. ChatGPT only said to 'check whether its controls tolerate the transfer time'.
decides: This supports the BLUETTI Elite 300, which BLUETTI rates at ≤10 ms, and the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 at 10 ms. Both switch over no slower than the 10 ms maximum of the UPS Harman approved. It is a reason to rank the Elite 200 V2 (15 ms), AC200L (20 ms), AC180 (20 ms) and ALLPOWERS P1800 (20 ms) lower as pass-through units, because 15–20 ms is slower than anything Harman tested. Our current page already lists those switchover times. There is a condition: transfer time only matters if the stove's own control is set to Continue Operation. With Harman's factory quick-shutdown setting, any power station just powers a shutdown. So the page should say: check the stove's power-failure setting first, then pick a unit that switches in ≤10 ms. This is our comparison; Harman publishes no ms limit.

findings.label: Harman default power-failure behaviour
findings.value: Controls 'pre-set for quick shutdown'; to keep heating, a dealer sets Continue Operation (dip switch #4 on knob-control boards); Rev E+ software (Nov 2010) pulses the blower on UPS power 'until the fire is out'
findings.source_title: Pellet Stove on a UPS: Shutdown Minutes or Hours of Heat? | Power Fallback
findings.note: This is in the cited Harman PDF, which Power Fallback quotes (HAR-0040U-0718), so a cited rival already has it. It sets the condition under which transfer time matters at all.
